acceptance: Both session-isolation tests pass on windows-latest 3.12, or carry a Windows skip with a stated reason
Linux and macOS locking is unchanged
context: Found by triage of the 2026-10-08 Windows 3.12 log. Developer tooling only; not release-blocking.
description: On Windows the session-isolation lock is msvcrt.locking(fd, LK_NBLCK, 1) on byte 0, and the holder text is also written at byte 0. A Windows byte-range lock is mandatory, so no other handle can read byte 0, even in the same process. Effects: tests/unit/test_session_isolation.py test_contended_lock_prevents_home_setup fails with PermissionError, and test_session_finish_restores_caller_environment waits to timeout because the child cannot read the holder pid and does not see the inherited lock. Fix: lock one byte far past the payload (for example os.lseek(fd, 1 << 30, os.SEEK_SET) before every msvcrt.locking call, with the same offset on unlock). Call sites: scripts/local_validation.py (the _close_lock unlock, wait_on_fd, clear_inactive_lock) and tests/utilities/session_isolation.py (two sites); replace the existing lseek(0) calls. write_holder is unaffected. Confirm on Windows that locking past EOF succeeds. Fallback if not worth fixing: Windows-skip both tests with a stated reason.
